items.prompt: Try this before I explain anything. White to move. Capture the one black piece that you can take for free.

claims.statement: The rook can slide up the file and take the knight.
The knight on d5 is the only loose black piece.
Taking the knight wins it for nothing.

hints: Which black piece is on a line your rook can travel along?
Look straight up the d-file from the rook.
The knight on d5 is the target.
items.explain: The rook on d1 looks up the d-file at the knight on d5. No black piece guards d5, so after the capture nothing can take the rook back.

items.prompt: White to move. Tap every loose black piece: attacked, and not defended.

claims.statement: Only the bishop on g4 is loose.
The pawn on h3 attacks the bishop.
No black piece defends the bishop.
The pawn on e6 defends the knight.
Nothing attacks the rook on a8.

hints: Start with the black pieces that a white piece attacks. There are two.
For each attacked piece, ask whether a black piece stands guard over it.
The pawn on e6 guards the knight. The bishop on g4 has no guard.
items.explain: The h3 pawn attacks the bishop and nothing guards it, so it is loose. The rook on d2 attacks the knight, but the e6 pawn defends it. The rook on a8 has no defender, yet nothing attacks it.

items.prompt: Black has just moved a knight to d6. Tap every loose WHITE piece.

claims.statement: Only the bishop on c4 is loose.
The knight on d6 attacks the bishop.
The pawn on g2 defends the knight on f3.
The bishop on g4 attacks the knight on f3.

hints: Look at which white pieces black pieces are pointing at.
Two white pieces are attacked. Check each one for a defender.
The knight on f3 is guarded by a pawn. The bishop on c4 is not guarded.
items.explain: The black knight on d6 attacks the bishop on c4, and no white piece defends it. The bishop on g4 attacks the knight on f3, but the pawn on g2 defends that knight.

items.prompt: White to move. Take the free piece with your knight.

claims.statement: The knight can jump to e6.
The bishop on e6 is loose.
Taking the bishop wins it for nothing.

hints: A knight attacks by jumping. Which black piece is one jump away?
The bishop stands on e6, a knight jump from d4.
Play the knight to e6.
items.explain: The knight on d4 jumps to e6 and takes the bishop. There is no black pawn on f7 to take back, so the knight is safe.

items.prompt: White to move. Does Rxd5 win a piece for free? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The queen on d8 defends the knight from far away.
Taking the knight loses the rook for a knight.
No black piece is loose.

hints: Trace each black piece's lines. Which one points at d5?
The queen on d8 looks down the d-file past the empty squares.
If the rook takes, the queen takes back.
items.explain: The queen on d8 sees the knight along the d-file, so it defends it. If the rook takes, the queen takes the rook: a rook (5) for a knight (3).

items.prompt: Now the reason. Which black piece defends the knight on d5? Tap it.

claims.statement: One black piece defends the knight.
The white rook attacks the knight.

hints: Trace the lines that end on d5.
Look along the d-file behind the knight.
The queen on d8 guards d5.
items.explain: The queen on d8 sees the knight along the d-file, so it defends it. That is why the rook cannot take for free.

items.prompt: White to move. Does Rxd5 win the knight? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Taking the knight wins it.
The knight is loose.
The king can step to f1, h1 or h2, and h2 is off the first row.

hints: Look at the first row after the rook leaves it.
Where could the king go if a black rook checked on the first row?
The h2 square is empty, so the king has a way out.
items.explain: The only change is that the pawn has moved to h3, so the king has the square h2. A check on the first row can be answered, and the rook wins the knight.

items.prompt: White to move. Is anything free to take?

claims.statement: The knight on d5 is loose.
The bishop on b7 is blocked by the knight on c6.
Taking the knight wins it.

hints: Which black pieces are attacked?
Does the bishop on b7 really see the knight? Look at the squares between.
The knight on c6 stands in the bishop's way.
items.explain: The bishop on b7 would defend d5, but its own knight on c6 blocks the diagonal, so d5 is undefended and the rook takes it for free.

items.prompt: Black has just moved a knight to c4. Which white piece can Black win for free? Tap it.

claims.statement: Only the pawn on b2 is loose.
The pawn on f2 defends the bishop on e3.
The knight on c4 attacks the bishop.

hints: Which white pieces does the knight on c4 attack?
The knight attacks a bishop and a pawn. Check both for defenders.
The f2 pawn guards the bishop. Nothing guards the b2 pawn.
items.explain: The knight on c4 attacks the bishop on e3 and the pawn on b2. The f2 pawn defends the bishop, but no white piece defends b2, so that pawn is loose.

items.prompt: White to move. Is anything free to take?

claims.statement: The rook on a6 defends the bishop along the sixth row.
Taking the bishop loses the rook for a bishop.
No black piece is loose.

hints: Which black piece is attacked?
Does anything defend the bishop, even from the far side?
Follow the sixth row from the bishop towards the left.
items.explain: The rook on a6 defends the bishop from the far side of the board. Taking it loses a rook for a bishop, so nothing is free.

items.prompt: Black to move. Does ...Rxd4 win a piece for free? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The rook wins the knight.
The knight on d4 is loose.

hints: Count the defenders of d4.
Nothing white guards d4, and the h6 pawn is irrelevant.
items.explain: The pawn move on h6 changes nothing: the knight is still attacked and undefended, so the rook takes it for free.
